paraphrase: The guru is the power (śakti); the body with its nine openings is the Śrīcakra; the channels are the powers of the cakra, the winds and elements its deities; the knower is the priest, knowledge the fire, the known the offering; worship is contemplation of non-difference.

checks.note: The content is located: śrīguruḥ sarvakāraṇabhūtā śaktiḥ; navarandhrarūpo dehaḥ; navaśaktirūpaṃ śrīcakram; jñātā hotā jñānam agnir jñeyaṃ haviḥ; abhedabhāvanaṃ śrīcakrapūjanam. The e-text is unnumbered. Tantrik Texts XI (1922, local eBhāratī copy) numbers the Bhāvanopaniṣad in ṛks.

paraphrase: The guru is the Śakti that is the cause of all; so the body with its nine openings is the Śrīcakra of nine cakras; Vārāhī is the father, Kurukullā the mother; the aims of life are the oceans; the body is the island of nine jewels; the fourteen channels are the deities of the fourteen triangles; the ten vital airs are the outer ten, the ten fires the inner ten; cold, heat, pleasure, pain, desire and the three qualities are Vaśinī and the other goddesses of speech; the five subtle elements are the five flower-arrows, mind the sugarcane bow, attachment the noose, aversion the goad; the unmanifest, mahat and ahaṃkāra are Kāmeśvarī, Vajreśvarī and Bhagamālinī in the inner triangle; the fifteen Nityās are the lunar days, the unfolding of time.

One who is thus absorbed in this contemplation for three muhūrtas becomes liberated while living; identity with the deity is accomplished; what he intends comes about without effort; he is called a Śiva-yogin. The bhāvanā has been taught according to the Kādi and Hādi doctrines.
The knower is the offerer (hotṛ), knowledge is the fire, the known is the oblation; contemplating the non-difference of knower, knowing and known is the worship of the Śrīcakra.

original.text: jñātā hotā jñānam agnir jñeyaṃ haviḥ / jñātṛjñānajñeyānām abhedabhāvanaṃ śrīcakrapūjanam

paraphrase: The offerings are inward: the readiness of the inner and outer senses is the invocation; their grasping one object the seat; the union of the three states the betel; the movement from the base to the crown and back the circumambulation; the fourth state the prostration; the immersion of the body-identified knower the bali-offering; the dissolving of 'is', 'is not', 'to be done' and 'not to be done' in the eternal self the fire-offering; immersion in her sandals the complete meditation.
